next_step: POC: VS Code extension hook + 1 week TTFT/kpi run; security questionnaire follow-up
notes:
Overview:
- Early-stage developer tools company building an IDE extension (VS Code + JetBrains) for realtime code completions and multi-line refactors. Primary UX target: completions returned while user is typing with near-zero interruption.

Technical requirements (emphasis):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token) target: <= 70ms median for local-typed completions; 95th < 200ms ideally.
- Low jitter critical: <20ms variance preferred to avoid cursor jumpiness.
- Sustained throughput: ~12k tokens/min per active developer seat during heavy editing sessions.
- Backpressure behavior: extension must gracefully degrade (show partial suggestion, spinner) rather than freeze editor. Need explicit streaming chunking and client-side buffering strategies.
- Token budget tuning: session-level budget to prevent runaway completions; dynamic truncation + soft stop when budget hits 80%.
- Model/version pinning: want stable completion behavior across releases; ability to route specific customers to pinned model versions for consistent logits.
- Hybrid routing: small/fast quantized model for immediate inline completions, fallback to larger model for multi-line or refactor suggestions. Automatic KV-cache warm-up when switching models.

Security & deployment notes:
- Prefer hosted API for quick start but want Dedicated/VPC for enterprise customers (SSO + audit log requirements).
- KMS integration required for encryption of customer telemetry and logs.
- Retention controls: ability to disable retention for certain enterprise orgs.

Timeline & activity log (shorthand):
- 2025-11-10: Lead created from meetup + demo sign-up.
- 2025-12-02: Intro call (Ava) — high-level product fit; interested in low-latency streaming.
- 2026-01-18: Deep-dive w/ SE (Marco) — shared VS Code extension architecture, sample telemetry. Asked about TTFT tuning knobs.
- 2026-02-05: Sent security questionnaire + Drive security FAQ.
- 2026-02-18: Product demo (recorded) — Fireflies ff-20260218-0582; notes: "Need fewer jitter spikes; small model for inline, big model for refactor".
- 2026-03-01: Bench harness v0 run (client-side synthetic typing). Results: median TTFT ~82ms, p95 ~240ms (needs improvement). Logged ticket RINF-4121 for kernel selection tuning.
- 2026-03-10: Sync — agreed POC: integrate Redwood streaming API into dev extension, run 7-day session with real devs, collect TTFT/jitter/throughput, and test token budget enforcement.

POC success criteria:
- Median TTFT <= 70ms, p95 < 200ms and jitter <20ms across sessions.
- No editor freezes observed during backpressure (manual QA + telemetry).
- Token budget controls prevent >2x baseline token consumption in 95% of sessions.
- Ability to pin model for control group with identical outputs across test period.

Quotes & paraphrases from stakeholders:
- "If the editor stutters even once during a demo, it kills adoption." — Head of Product.
- "We need a hard kill switch on long-running completions at the client side." — Lead Engineer.

Open questions for Redwood:
- Can Redwood expose per-session token budget APIs + early stop signals via SSE/stream metadata?
- How much control do we have over chunk size / flush frequency on streaming responses?
- Will Dedicated provide the deterministic p95 SLA needed for enterprise customers?

Next actions (short):
- SE (Marco) to share recommended runtime config (batching, kernel hints, quant profile) by 2026-03-14.
- Engineering to start VS Code POC hook (auth + streaming client) this week.
- Security to review KMS integration plan; follow-up meeting 2026-03-16.

Misc:
- Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching thresholds and token-budget defaults.
- Will run A/B comparing model-pinned behavior vs rolling default in week 2 of POC.

CRM notes style: short bullets, action items, and occasional direct quotes. Revisit after POC for updated forecast.
